Agreement between the People's Republic of China and the Republic of Singapore for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (as revised on 8 November 2024, effective 1 January 2025); Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Owner Information (promulgated by the People's Bank of China and the State Administration for Market Regulation, Order No. 3 [2024], effective 1 November 2024); Measures for the Administration of Enterprise Name Registration (State Council, effective 1 March 2021); Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China and its Implementing Regulations; and relevant PBOC customer due diligence and transaction record-keeping rules as amended.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of Foreign Corporate Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or registrar in the foreign shareholder's home jurisdiction (e.g., Hong Kong Companies Registry, ACRA, Companies House, Delaware Division of Corporations)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel and mutually exclusive route: notarize locally, then obtain a Hague Apostille from the home jurisdiction's designated Competent Authority for Apostille Convention member states; for non-member states, notarize locally and then complete Consular Legalization through the competent Chinese Embassy or Consulate. Apostille and Consular Legalization must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Existence of Foreign Corporate Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or registrar in the foreign shareholder's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel and mutually exclusive route: notarize locally, then obtain a Hague Apostille; for non-Hague members, use Consular Legalization by the Chinese Embassy or Consulate. Never apply Apostille and Consular Legalization sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney Authorizing WFOE Formation, Signatories and Bank Account Opening
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary, notary public, or authorized officer of the foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel and mutually exclusive route: notarize the signature and corporate capacity, then either (i) Hague Apostille for Apostille Convention states, or (ii) Consular Legalization for non-member states. No chain of apostille followed by legalization is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum and Articles of Association / Constitutional Documents of Foreign Corporate Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry, corporate secretary, or registered agent of the foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel and mutually exclusive route: certified true copy notarized locally followed by Hague Apostille where applicable; otherwise Consular Legalization by the Chinese Embassy or Consulate. The two authentication mechanisms are alternatives and must not be sequentially combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from Foreign Corporate Shareholder's Relationship Bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Relationship bank or branch manager of the foreign corporate shareholder's bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel and mutually exclusive route: bank officer signature notarized locally, then Hague Apostille; for non-Hague jurisdictions, notarization followed by Consular Legalization at the Chinese Embassy or Consulate. Do not apply both apostille and consular legalization to the same instrument.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency / Register of Directors and Shareholders of Foreign Corporate Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or registered agent of the foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel and mutually exclusive route: notarization locally followed by Hague Apostille for member states; for non-member states, notarization followed by Consular Legalization through the Chinese Embassy or Consulate. These routes are mutually exclusive and must not be chained.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening must cover every UBO above 25%, director, supervisor, senior manager, authorized signatory, and material payment counterparty. Screening must be executed against the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, PRC MFA designated persons and entities lists, SAMR and PBOC AML/market-entry blacklists, PRC dishonest debtor list, and OFAC SDN, EU, UK and other sanctions lists where foreign currency, correspondent banking, or payment rails such as Stripe and Affirm are used. PEP identification must include immediate family and close associates, with enhanced due diligence, source of wealth, and source of funds verification before submission.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: SAMR National Enterprise Name Registration System (Enterprise Name Self-Service Declaration Portal) via the provincial integrated online government service platform
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered Chinese company name must be composed of simplified Chinese characters and follow the four-tier statutory naming convention: administrative division + distinctive trade name (zihao) + industry/operation characteristics + organizational form (Limited Liability Company). Foreign Latin-script names and Pinyin transliterations are supplementary only and cannot be used as the legal registered Chinese name. Non-Chinese investor names must be transliterated into standard Putonghua Pinyin; the chosen trade name must be unique within the relevant industry and administrative region and must not mislead the public as to the company's nature, scale, or regulatory status.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within the initial 30-day reservation window, the applicant may request a one-time 30-day extension before expiry or reapply after rectification. Upon rejection, the applicant must obtain a written rejection notice stating the statutory grounds. The applicant may file an administrative reconsideration application with the higher market regulation authority or SAMR within 60 days of receiving the rejection notice, and may later bring an administrative lawsuit within 6 months if reconsideration fails. Counsel should preserve all time-stamped submission screenshots, reference numbers, and rejection correspondence.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office or commercial mail-forwarding box is not permissible as the sole registered address for a WFOE. SAMR registration requires proof of a physical address in China, typically an original property ownership certificate or a registered lease agreement. Tax registration and VAT invoicing verification use the same physical address, and banks require an on-site KYC inspection before account activation. For ISIC 4791 direct online retail of solar portable power products, no retail storefront is required, but approved address hosting in free-trade zones or government-designated industrial parks may be used only where the competent management committee issues an official address certificate and a physical operational presence is maintained or independently verifiable.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Likelihood of unannounced physical inspection is moderate: SAMR 'double random, one disclosure' inspection probability is approximately 10-20% annually for a newly registered WFOE; municipal tax verification visits run approximately 15-25% in the first operating year; bank KYC site visits occur in 70-90% of account opening cases; PBOC field audits are low probability but non-zero. Checklist: (i) registered nameplate posted; (ii) original lease and property certificates maintained; (iii) actual office furniture and staff presence; (iv) VAT and tax-system access available; (v) management, HR and internal controls records available on site; (vi) bank and SAMR correspondence received at the registered address without reliance on a mail-forward box.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: SAMR enterprise name clearance and company registration filing fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation / local Administration for Market Regulation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No official registration fee is charged under current statutory tariff; fee is nil.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Beneficial owner information filing through PBOC/SAMR system
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: PBOC and SAMR Beneficial Owner Information System
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory filing fee; fee is nil.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Foreign corporate document notarization for six instruments in home jurisdiction
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign notary public and home-jurisdiction corporate secretary or agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark and notarial tariff in the document's country of origin.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization of foreign corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Home-jurisdiction Apostille Competent Authority or Chinese Embassy/Consulate where Consular Legalization applies
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee schedule of the issuing authority; market benchmark for processing and courier.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Simplified Chinese translation of apostilled/legalized document bundle
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: PRC certified translation company and PRC law firm review
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per page after source-country legalization.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PRC legal counsel due diligence, name clearance handling, corporate governance review and legal opinion
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: PRC law firm retained by the foreign investor
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing PRC market benchmark for cross-border WFOE formation; fixed or hourly fee.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office address or approved address hosting arrangement for first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Landlord, commercial property provider, free-trade zone management committee or permitted address hosting operator
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for qualified physical registered office or park-based hosting.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Administrative assistance for tax registration, bank pre-scoping and corporate seal coordination
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: PRC local service provider and/or law firm in coordination with SAMR and tax authorities
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for formation support services, notarial seal costs and translation if separately invoiced.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision), effective 1 July 2024, Articles 1-47 and 152-164 (establishment, capital, organizational structure); Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019), Articles 1-42; Regulations on the Implementation of the Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (State Council Decree No. 723); Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Registration Administration of Market Entities (State Council Decree No. 746), Articles 1-57
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), with delegated execution by the local Municipal Market Supervision Administration at the registered domicile; online filing via the National Integrated Online Government Service Platform and the SAMR Market Entity Registration service
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Establishment Registration of a Foreign-Invested Limited Liability Company, together with the Articles of Association and the sole shareholder's written decision
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no blocked escrow account requirement for a general trading WFOE under the 2023 Company Law. Shareholders may stipulate the registered capital amount and payment schedule in the Articles of Association. Registered capital must be authentic and paid in within the agreed period. Under foreign exchange regulation, inbound equity contributions must be credited to a designated capital contribution account after the bank has completed the SAFE FDI registration, and paid-in capital amounts must be reflected in the Market Entity Annual Report.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF CN_WFOE_LTD: RESOLVED, that CN_WFOE_LTD (the Company) shall be incorporated as a wholly foreign-owned enterprise under the Company Law of the People's Republic of China, with limited liability and registered office at the address identified in the Articles of Association, being the address to be filed with the local Market Supervision Administration, and that the legal representative shall execute and submit every instrument required for registration. RESOLVED, that the registered capital of the Company is authorized at RMB [amount] or USD [amount] as stated in the Articles, and that the sole shareholder, [name], subscribes the full registered capital subject to payment on or before the date set in the Articles; no preferred shares, options, warrants, or debt instruments may be issued without a further shareholder resolution. RESOLVED, that the principal bank account of the Company shall be opened with [Bank], [Branch], and the legal representative together with any director or manager appointed by the board is hereby authorized, jointly or severally, to complete account opening, mandated signatory, online banking, remittance, currency conversion, capital contribution account, and bank anti-money-laundering and know-your-client documentation and to execute related forms. RESOLVED, that [name] is appointed executive director and legal representative of the Company, [name] is appointed supervisor, and [name] is appointed general manager, each to serve from the date of registration until a successor is duly appointed. RESOLVED, that the appointed officers are authorized to execute bank mandates, tax registration, customs registration, social insurance filings, housing fund filings, lease contracts for the registered office, and all employment contracts and third-party agreements necessary to commence lawful operations. RESOLVED, that this resolution is effective immediately and may be executed in counterparts, and the legal representative is directed to register the Company, to arrange publication and publicity as required by law, and to take all ancillary actions necessary to give full effect to these resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Pre-approval and Foreign Investor Document Legalization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Municipal Market Supervision Administration (SAMR) enterprise name registration windows, or the National Integrated Online Government Service Platform at gjzwfw.gov.cn
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before filing the incorporation application, the foreign shareholder must secure an approved corporate name in the format Administrative Division plus Trade Name plus Trade Description plus Limited Liability Company. The applicant must log onto the SAMR online platform or attend the local service hall, complete the enterprise name pre-approval form, designate the legal representative and supervisor, and upload a notarized and apostilled certificate of incorporation for the foreign shareholder. All foreign-language documents must be accompanied by a certified Chinese translation. SAMR conducts name conflict screening against the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System and reserves the approved name for six months pending establishment registration.
required_dossiers: Application for Enterprise Name Reservation
Notarized and Apostilled Certificate of Incorporation or Certificate of Good Standing of the foreign shareholder
Passport or other government-issued identification of the proposed legal representative
Power of attorney appointing the formation agent
Certified Chinese translation of all foreign documents
Letter of intent or draft lease for the proposed registered address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected because of duplication, similarity to protected marks, or prohibited words, the applicant should propose at least three alternative names and re-file through the same portal within five working days; if the reviewer requires additional ownership documentation, upload a board resolution of the foreign investor and a new apostille; if the translation is defective, replace it with a certified translation and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Execution and Apostille or Notarization of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Competent apostille authority of the foreign shareholder's home country under the Hague Apostille Convention, with subsequent review and translation support by licensed PRC formation counsel; for non-Convention states, notarization and PRC Consular Legalization
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Formation counsel prepares the Articles of Association, the sole shareholder's written decision, the first board resolution, the appointment of the legal representative and supervisor, and the registered address documents in accordance with the Company Law and Foreign Investment Law. The foreign shareholder must execute the Articles in counterpart before a notary if requested by the bank or SAMR. Since China is a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, foreign public documents must be apostilled; where no apostille exists, the longer notarization and consular legalization chain is required. After signing, every document is translated into Chinese by a certified translator, and the notarized and apostilled package is bound and kept ready for the establishment registration.
required_dossiers: Apostilled Certificate of Incorporation of the foreign investor
Apostilled board resolution of the foreign investor authorizing establishment of the PRC WFOE
Original certified Chinese translation of the Articles of Association signed by the sole shareholder
Power of attorney with express authority to sign all PRC formation documents
Copy of the foreign investor's latest audited financial statements or bank reference, where requested
Identification documents of the appointed PRC legal representative and supervisor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SAMR queries authenticity, the formation counsel must arrange re-notarization or supplementary apostille; if the Power of Attorney lacks specificity, a new Power of Attorney with express authority to sign all PRC filings must be executed, notarized, apostilled, translated, and resubmitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment Registration and Business License Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Municipal Market Supervision Administration (SAMR) service center for market entity registration, or the provincial Government Service Network portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the establishment registration by submitting the completed Application for Establishment Registration of a Foreign-Invested Limited Liability Company, the original certified Articles, and all apostilled investor documents. The registration official will review the registered capital, business scope, legal representative, statutory supervisor, and registered address; ordinary WFOE capital contributions are not blocked or escrowed. Registration must be completed before any bank account is operated. Once approved, SAMR issues a Business License with a Unified Social Credit Code, which constitutes the company's legal personality. The company should verify that the business scope includes internet retail sales of solar power generation equipment and portable electric energy storage equipment, and import and export if cross-border purchases are intended.
required_dossiers: Application for Establishment Registration signed by the legal representative and sole shareholder
Original certified Articles of Association
Apostilled Certificate of Incorporation and apostilled good standing certificate of the foreign investor, with certified Chinese translation
Lease contract and certificate of property ownership or landlord consent for the registered address
Passport copies of the legal representative, supervisors, and directors
Appointment letters for directors, supervisor, and general manager
Enterprise Name Pre-approval Notice
Power of attorney appointing the PRC formation agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SAMR returns the application as suspended or under substantive verification, answer the query in writing within the prescribed time limit, rectify any inconsistency between the business scope and the Articles, update lease or address proof, and refile; if refusal is issued, the applicant may take administrative reconsideration to the next higher SAMR within 60 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Formalities: Seal Carving, Bank Accounts, Tax, Social Insurance and Customs
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Security Bureau licensed seal engraving unit; local branch of the State Taxation Administration; local social insurance and medical insurance bureaus; designated bank branch for RMB and foreign currency accounts; General Administration of Customs for customs registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within ten days after the Business License is issued, obtain the company seal, financial seal, invoice seal, and legal representative seal from a PSB-licensed engraver and file the seal registration with the Public Security Bureau. Open a basic deposit account at the bank selected by the board and, for foreign currency capital, a capital contribution account; the bank will file the FDI foreign exchange registration with SAFE. Register for tax withholding and value-added tax status at the local tax office, enroll in the electronic tax invoicing system, and file the financial accounting system and accounting software. Complete social insurance, housing fund, employment registration, and statistical reporting. If the WFOE will import portable battery generators and solar panels, apply for customs registration and a customs declaration code with the General Administration of Customs; lithium batteries may require UN38.3 test certificates and CCC or voluntary product certification as applicable.
required_dossiers: Business License and Unified Social Credit Code certificate
Articles of Association and first board resolution
Official, financial, invoice, and legal representative seals with PSB seal record
Legal representative and officer identification documents
Board resolution authorizing bank signatories and account operators
Power of attorney for tax agents and customs declarants
Lease contract for the registered office
FDI Foreign Exchange Registration Form, where the bank requires it
Business scope code list for customs and e-commerce reporting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to open a capital account due to incomplete SAFE records, contact SAFE through the bank to update foreign investment information; if the tax bureau flags missing local filings, submit the financial accounting system documentation and revised registration; any noncompliance can be cured through a supplementary filing and, where unavoidable, a minor late-filing penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Information Reporting, E-Commerce Compliance and Annual Mandatory Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Commerce through the Foreign Investment Information Reporting System integrated into SAMR; State Administration of Foreign Exchange through authorized banks; Ministry of Industry and Information Technology through the provincial communications administration for ICP filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 days after incorporation, the investor or the WFOE must submit the foreign investment information report through the system integrated into SAMR, including beneficial ownership information, investment amount, and business scope. This report satisfies the foreign investment information reporting obligation under the Foreign Investment Law. The company must appoint a designated person to complete the Market Entity Annual Report before June 30 on the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System. For e-commerce operations, the WFOE must ensure the Business License covers online retail and, if it operates its own website instead of using a third-party marketplace, obtain an ICP filing with the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology through the provincial communications administration. Payment rails such as Stripe and Affirm are not directly operated by the PRC legal entity; the company should use approved cross-border payment institutions and may need a trade or financial reporting code under SAFE for inbound and outbound settlement.
required_dossiers: Business License
Foreign Investment Information Report Form
FDI registration certificate issued by the authorized bank
Market Entity Annual Report form and standing authorization
Articles of Association and board resolution on e-commerce compliance
Proof of ICP filing if operating an independent website
Cross-border payment institution agreement, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the foreign investment information report is rejected, correct the mismatched investment amount and re-file; if the annual report deadline is missed, apply to SAMR for reopening or submit a written explanation; if the ICP filing is suspended, supplement the domain certificate and server hosting contract and resubmit through the provincial communications administration.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - no manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing activities under ISIC 4791; the competent product and market safety authority for the online retail business is the State Administration for Market Regulation, and the General Administration of Customs for imported solar panels and battery products
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - ISIC 4791 online retail of portable battery generators and solar panels does not require an industrial operating permit or production license; the WFOE does not operate a physical plant or warehouse, although imported products must still satisfy CCC certification, RoHS, electronic waste, and UN38.3 transport-safety requirements where applicable

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Ecology and Environment of the People's Republic of China
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - retail trade under ISIC 4791 does not appear in the 2021 Classified Management List of Environmental Impact Assessment for Construction Projects; no EIA registration, environmental impact statement, or full EIA report is required in the absence of construction, manufacturing, or chemical processing activity
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to pure online retail operations. If the company later adds warehousing, battery assembly, or other physical operations, it must comply with the Integrated Wastewater Discharge Standard GB 8978-1996, the Integrated Emission Standard of Air Pollutants GB 16297-1996, and the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Prevention and Control of Environmental Pollution by Solid Waste, including hazardous waste identification, manifest, and disposal requirements for spent lithium batteries.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for a pure online retail office and no physical production or storage facility. If the company later leases or uses a distribution warehouse, it must complete fire protection acceptance or fire safety record-filing with the local Fire and Rescue Division, maintain fire prevention measures under GB 50016-2014, obtain a Building Fire Safety Inspection Certificate or prior filing, and complete occupational safety and health registration with the local Emergency Management Bureau.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China; online portal is the Unified Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax Bureau), operated nationally by the STA and provincially by local offices, accessible through the STA's official website and local tax service portals.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the WFOE, tax registration is integrated with market registry formalities. After issuance of the business license bearing the 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), the enterprise tax registry is automatically populated by the State Taxation Administration via interoperability with the State Administration for Market Regulation. The USCC serves as the enterprise's statutory Tax Identification Number (TIN) and VAT payer identification number. Foreign non-resident enterprises, where they have no permanent establishment but derive Chinese-source income, must apply for a non-resident enterprise taxpayer identity through the competent STA office where the withholding agent is located, or where the income arises, by submitting a tax residence certificate issued by the country of residence, an application for tax registration, and the underlying contract or agreement evidencing Chinese-source income. The STA will then issue a non-resident taxpayer identifier in the form of a tax identification number embedded in the system for withholding reporting.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The People's Republic of China does not operate a check-the-box entity classification regime comparable to the United States, and no hybrid mismatch elections are available. Enterprise income tax classification follows the Enterprise Income Tax Law's resident enterprise and non-resident enterprise dichotomy, supplemented by the special tax adjustment and controlled foreign corporation rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: All enterprises carrying on business in China must complete VAT registration immediately upon issuance of the business license; there is no monthly minimum threshold to register. A turnover threshold of RMB 5,000,000 in annual taxable sales triggers mandatory classification as a general VAT taxpayer, while presumptive or small-scale taxpayer status applies below that threshold with simplified collection rates.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China operates a mandatory national electronic invoice control regime under the Golden Tax Phase IV system and the Unified E-Invoice Service Platform. VAT invoices, including fully digitised electronic invoices (FDEI), must be issued in real time through STA-authorised systems; invoice metadata, recipient details, and amounts are transmitted to the STA electronically at the moment of issuance. All newly registered enterprises, including WFOEs, must complete FDEI configuration in the e-Tax Bureau before issuing VAT invoices. No offline invoice creation or manual fiscal stamping is permitted for general VAT taxpayers engaged in retail e-commerce.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating of VAT applies to exported goods, including portable battery generators and solar panels, where the taxpayer with general VAT status sells and physically ships the goods from mainland China to a foreign buyer outside the customs territory. Eligibility is established when the customs authority releases the goods under an export declaration reflecting the export enterprise, commodity HS code, quantity, and destination. Cross-border e-commerce retail exports may use the special cross-border e-commerce export regime, which likewise grants a 0% VAT rate and, in appropriate designated markets, export VAT rebates if the goods are shipped from a registered bonded warehouse or declared through the e-commerce retail export channel. The taxpayer must maintain contemporaneous records of the transaction, platform sales opulence trading, logistics trail, and foreign exchange receipts to demonstrate authentic cross-border trade.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Goods Declaration submitted via the China International Trade Single Window with electronic release data
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or international courier shipment manifest covering the entire carriage
Bank foreign exchange receipt record and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) export proceeds verification demonstrating repatriation
Commercial invoice, packing list, and sale contract or platform purchase order
VAT export rebate electronic application e-file submitted through the e-Tax Bureau export tax rebate module
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are scrutinised by the STA against customs release data, bank foreign exchange settlement records, and logistics information. In the event of a false declaration, fraudulent VAT invoice use, failure to collect or repatriate export proceeds, or inability to substantiate the zero-rated export, the taxpayer is liable to repay any VAT refund or zero-rated input credit claimed, pay a daily late payment surcharge of 0.05% on the outstanding tax, and be subject to a monetary penalty of between 50% and 500% of the tax evaded under Article 63 of the Tax Administration Law of the People's Republic of China. Criminal accountability for export VAT refund fraud or fraudulent issuance of VAT invoices may also attach under the Criminal Law, and the responsible persons may additionally be placed on the State Taxation Administration's list of seriously dishonest taxpayers.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBoC) and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) of the People's Republic of China
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Chinese renminbi is fully convertible on the current account for bona fide trade and service transactions once the underlying economic activity is verified under SAFE's trade authenticity framework. Capital account convertibility, however, remains administratively controlled. A Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) receiving FDI equity injections must first complete foreign exchange registration with SAFE through a designated domestic bank, open a capital account foreign currency settlement account, and register each inward remittance. Proceeds converted into RMB under the capital account settlement mechanism must be used within the entity's business scope on a positive-list basis; prohibited outflows include domestic equity investment, lending, trust financial products, and non-operating real estate purchases unless separately licensed. Profit repatriation is treated as a current-account remittance after compliance with tax law: the WFOE must present certification of annual audits, tax clarity certificates, profit reserve accrual evidence, and audited financial statements to the remitting bank, which will verify the amount and SAFE registration. Dividends are legally distributable only after corporate income tax settlement and required reserve provisions. The surrendering requirement for export proceeds has been progressively liberalized, but trade-related foreign exchange receipts must be repatriated into China, and their authenticity must be supported by customs declarations, logistics documents, and invoices before conversion. A WFOE engaged in cross-border e-commerce retail must therefore build accounting infrastructure that reconciles platform receivables, export declarations, and foreign exchange receipts in real time to withstand bank and SAFE scrutiny.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: China no longer imposes a mandatory foreign exchange surrender ratio or a compulsory conversion rate on export receipts. Under SAFE's trade in goods administration rules, all export proceeds from a WFOE must be repatriated into a domestic current-account foreign exchange settlement account unless SAFE has approved an offshore foreign exchange account for specific trade structures. The enterprise may choose to retain 100% of export proceeds in foreign currency or convert them into RMB through the designated bank. Repatriation timing is generally required within 90 days after the export customs declaration date, with a possible extension to 180 days for enterprises on SAFE's approved whitelist or for established recurring trade patterns. Each export settlement transaction must be matched against the export collection and verification system, supported by the electronic customs declaration, commercial invoice, airway bill or bill of lading, and platform transaction records where applicable, before the bank processes the conversion.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of China Limited (Head Office, Corporate Banking Division)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited (ICBC)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account / Export Proceeds Settlement Account
Capital Settlement Account / Operational RMB Account
Trade Settlement and Export Collection Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Fintech electronic money institutions and offshore digital EMI platforms have low feasibility as primary treasury rails for a Chinese WFOE. Chinese banking law requires an entity's statutory corporate account and capital verification process to be held with a licensed domestic commercial bank that reports directly to PBoC and SAFE. Offshore EMIs are not licensed to hold the WFOE's RMB capital account, receive FDI equity injections, or issue the foreign exchange registration certificate required by SAFE. EMIs such as Airwallex, Currenxie, or Payoneer may be used only as ancillary collection tools for overseas e-commerce platform proceeds and cannot legally replace a domestic bank account for statutory capital, taxation, customs, audit, or dividend remittance purposes. Their ability to service a Chinese-domiciled entity is legally constrained because they do not hold a China banking or payment institution license necessary for local safekeeping of RMB, and any cross-border settlement they facilitate must ultimately be routed through a domestic designated bank that performs SAFE filing and AML screening. Therefore, the WFOE must prioritize a Tier-1 domestic bank as the primary banking counterparty and treat EMIs merely as secondary payment aggregation rails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Chinese commercial banks generally require the WFOE's legal representative, at least one director or senior officer with actual signing authority, and the financial controller to appear physically at the branch to open a corporate account and complete the compliance interview. Remote opening is not fully recognized for a newly registered WFOE; however, a hybrid arrangement is possible where the legal representative executes a notarized Power of Attorney in the jurisdiction of residence, the POA and corporate documents are legalized through the Chinese embassy or consulate, and the authorized attorney-in-fact physically attends the bank together with the company stamp and a video call confirmation from the legal representative. Some Tier-1 banks may permit a video interview after documentary verification if the foreign shareholder's home jurisdiction has no Chinese consular post, but this is discretionary and does not override the bank's need to validate the seat of the company. The statutory directors of the WFOE should also be prepared to provide personal identification in original form, proof of address, source of wealth summaries, and a written explanation of the commercial purpose of the account, because foreign-controlled trading entities are subject to enhanced review regardless of the low-risk designation of the industry.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate Beneficial Ownership opacity involving a foreign corporate shareholder or intermediary holding company located in a low-tax jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A completed UBO declaration form identifying all natural persons above 25% direct or indirect ownership; certified copies of the shareholder's certificate of incorporation and articles of association; a full chain of ownership chart from the ultimate individual to the WFOE; audited financial statements or net asset proof of the foreign shareholder; a sworn source of wealth and source of funds statement; and passport copies of all UBOs, with notarization and consular legalization where required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ambiguity in the company's actual physical operating presence because the WFOE is used as an e-commerce shell with only a registered address and no substantive warehouse or personnel in China
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A valid and registered office lease agreement with a term covering at least 12 months; utility bills in the WFOE's name; an employee payroll record and social insurance statements; photographs or video walkthrough of the premises showing inventory storage for solar portable power products; a detailed staffing organigram; and the WFOE's business license showing the approved operational scope aligned with ISIC 4791 online retail.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border settlement traffic from third-party payment platforms including Stripe and Affirm BNPL that creates commingled funds or obscures the underlying retail transaction identity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed platform operating agreements with Stripe and Affirm along with the merchant identification numbers; complete transaction-level reconciliation reports showing payer ID, order ID, product description, quantity, price, tax, shipping destination, and payment conversion currency; the WFOE's export customs declaration records matching online orders; an internal AML/transaction review manual; and a third-party audit letter confirming no prohibited payment types or sanctions exposure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Silkroad or dual-use concern arising from export of solar-powered battery products that may contain lithium-ion batteries and specialized charging electronics
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Material Safety Data Sheets and UN38.3 battery transportation test reports; IEC or UL certification documents for the portable power generators; a product technical specification sheet demonstrating the absence of military or missile-related applications; supplier list and purchase invoices for battery cells and solar panels; a written confirmation from the customs broker that the HS classification is not controlled under China's export control list; and a bank-compatible compliance warranty from the WFOE stating the goods are civilian consumer retail items.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The foreign parent must execute the FDI equity injection by remitting the capital contribution through SWIFT MT103 or a similar cross-border wire to the WFOE's SAFE-registered capital account at the designated domestic bank. The remittance must carry the correct foreign exchange nature code for foreign direct investment equity contributions, namely the domestic bank's FDI registration number and the SAFE filing reference; the bank will then perform a rigorous verification of the amount against the registered capital quota. Upon receipt of the foreign currency, the WFOE must engage a certified public accountant to issue a capital verification report confirming that the contribution has been fully settled into the domestic capital account and that the use of converted RMB is confined to approved business operations as per SAFE's positive list. For each conversion, the WFOE must submit the business registration certificate, the bank's foreign exchange registration form, the capital verification report, and a genuine payment order such as a payroll list, supplier invoice, or logistics contract. No inbound investment may be routed through an offshore EMI or through personal accounts, and any conversion must be executed at the designated bank's counter rate or through the bank's FX dealing platform.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The WFOE should use SWIFT MT103 for direct supplier payments, freight forwarder settlement, and small-value operating expenses in foreign currencies. For purchase of battery packs, solar panels, or inverters from suppliers requiring payment against documents, the entity can issue an Irrevocable Letter of Credit at sight or usance, governed by UCP600, confirmed by a reputable Chinese issuing bank and advised by the beneficiary's overseas bank. Documentary collections may be used for intra-group or repeat supplier transactions where trust levels are established, but they carry higher payment risk and should be limited to low-value shipments. For cross-border RMB payments to suppliers in Belt and Road or RMB-clearing jurisdictions, the WFOE can use CIPS-Payment Instruction or SWIFT MT103 with CNY settlement through its domestic bank's cross-border RMB clearing line. All outbound payments must be accompanied by the underlying import contract, customs declaration, invoice, and logistics proof, and must satisfy the bank's current-account authenticity review before the bank is permitted to debit the entity's settlement account.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CNY foreign exchange forward contracts with a licensed domestic bank, based on genuine current-account trade exposure and supported by export or import documentation
Foreign exchange swaps between CNY and USD/EUR conducted at the onshore interbank market through the designated domestic bank, limited to cash flow hedging of known trade receivables or payables
Cross-currency interest rate or principal swap structures approved by SAFE for long-term capital account obligations, only where the underlying WFOE debt or receivables are verified
FX options or zero-cost structures involving call and put combinations traded onshore, provided they are for hedging and not for proprietary speculation

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are generally not permissible for onshore WFOE entities because onshore forward contracts are deliverable; NDF access is reserved for non-resident counterparties and may not be booked directly by the Chinese WFOE

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Enterprise Annual Credit Report (Annual Report Filing) including the Foreign Investment Information Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System, coordinated with Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) for foreign investment data
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 to June 30 of each calendar year for the preceding fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file by June 30 causes the enterprise to be listed in the Directory of Enterprises with Abnormal Operations within 10 working days; if not rectified within 3 years, the Market Regulation Administration may revoke the business license (administrative strike-off) and blacklist the legal representative. Civil and administrative remedies include fines and restrictions on bank settlement and invoicing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Final Settlement and Declaration (Annual CIT Reconciliation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) and the competent local tax authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before May 31 following each fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing is punishable by a fine of RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000; late payment accrues a daily surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid tax amount. Persistent default triggers enforced collection, asset attachment, and the withholding of export refunds or issuing of invoices under the tax enforcement law.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Compulsory for all WFOEs and limited liability companies irrespective of turnover, balance sheet size, or headcount. Under Article 164 of the PRC Company Law, each company must engage a licensed CPA firm in China to audit its annual financial report. No quantitative exemption exists for small or below-threshold private retail enterprises; the requirement is universal. For foreign-invested enterprises, the annual foreign investment information reporting framework further expects an audit report to substantiate financial and operational filings. Specialized quantitative thresholds apply only to public-interest entities and listed companies, not to a private WFOE engaged in online retail.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (ASBE) - substantially converged with IFRS, administered by the Ministry of Finance. The Enterprise Accounting Standards - Small Entities may apply only if the entity clearly qualifies as a small enterprise under the Chinese definition and the company chooses to adopt it; however, for a WFOE under normal online retail activity, the full ASBE is the default and expected statutory framework. Financial statements must be prepared in RMB and in Chinese.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the PRC Market Entity Beneficial Owner Registration Measures (effective 1 March 2024), a WFOE must file beneficial ownership information with the Market Regulation Administration at incorporation and must report any change in beneficial ownership within 30 days of the date the change occurs. The enterprise annual report, filed through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System between January 1 and June 30, includes a mandatory section to reconfirm the previously registered beneficial ownership information. Failure to update within the 30-day window or to accurately reconfirm in the annual report exposes the entity to administrative fines of up to RMB 50,000, and responsible directors or officers to personal fines of up to RMB 20,000.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors, Supervisors and Senior Executives
Register of Charges over Assets (Equity Pledges and Movable Property)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 - USD 3,000 per year for a registered address or corporate secretarial agent service in tier-2 or tier-3 Chinese cities; tier-1 cities may range higher
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000 - USD 6,000 for a small-to-medium online retail WFOE, assuming simple cross-border structure and moderate transaction volume

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: A Mainland China WFOE is subject to the uniform statutory Enterprise Income Tax (EIT) rate of 25%. Preferential regimes include: (i) 15% reduced rate for qualifying High and New Technology Enterprises; (ii) effective 5% tax rate for Small Low-Profit Enterprises with taxable income up to RMB 3 million per annum; (iii) 100% additional super deduction for qualifying R&D expenses; (iv) 15% rate available under certain encouraged-industry free-trade-zone or western-region policies where applicable. Ordinary online retail does not receive an automatic tax holiday. VAT export zero-rating for cross-border e-commerce does not alter EIT liability.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: China Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return (Form A, Form Code A200000) filed electronically through the State Taxation Administration e-Tax portal of the local competent tax authority.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final filing with quarterly provisional filings and tax prepayments during the year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return and final settlement of tax must be filed and paid within five months after the fiscal year end (31 May for a calendar-year WFOE). Quarterly prepayments must be filed and paid within 15 days after the end of each quarter.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1: Taxpayer Identification and Filing Status
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal English name of the WFOE, Unified Social Credit Code, fiscal year, registered address, industry classification, registered capital, shareholder information, and business status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose the foreign parent entity, jurisdiction of tax residence, percentage ownership, and OECD tax identification number. Confirm PRC taxation as a resident enterprise. Do not mark the entity as dormant or inactive if e-commerce sales continue. This form is the corporate income tax return, not the VAT return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2: Accounting Basis, Financial Reporting Standard and Functional Currency
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Indicates PRC Accounting Standards, accrual basis, going-concern assumption, RMB as reporting currency, and whether the financial statements are audited.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Convert all foreign-currency e-commerce proceeds and intercompany balances into RMB using the applicable tax-recognized exchange rate. Reconcile book foreign-exchange gains and losses with Box 7. Parent-company consolidation adjustments are irrelevant for PRC taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3: Operating Revenue from Online Retail
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross sales revenue from direct online retail of portable solar generators, solar panels, battery storage equipment, and accessories. Include revenue settled through Stripe, Affirm BNPL, and other payment rails.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not offset revenue by inventory costs or platform fees. Match reported revenue with bank settlement files, customs export declarations, and platform sales reports. Deferred revenue related to warranty and after-sales obligations must be recognized in accordance with contract terms. Undeclared sales will constitute tax evasion.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Inventory cost of sold units, inbound freight, import duties, warehouse storage, and directly allocable logistics costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For imports purchased from a related foreign manufacturer or distributor, the customs value and book cost must satisfy the arm's length principle. Maintain consistent inventory costing methodology. Abnormal inventory losses require tax filing and approval; otherwise they are nondeductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5: Selling, Administrative, R&D and Financial Expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Platform commissions, digital advertising, payment-processing fees, payroll, rent, depreciation, banking charges, logistics, regulatory compliance, and research or product-development costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Related-party management fees, service fees, and royalties are deductible only when the services were actually rendered, are commercially reasonable, and are supported by contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation. Entertainment expense is capped at 60% of the total incurred and 0.5% of annual revenue. Qualifying R&D expenditure may enjoy a 100% super deduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net operating result before non-operating items, as shown in the outer-accounting profit schedule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile directly to the WFOE audited financial statements. Show a benchmark return consistent with the economically important functions performed in China. Persistent book losses while paying high management or royalty fees to foreign affiliates will trigger transfer pricing examination and potential deemed profit adjustment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7: Non-Operating Income, Non-Operating Expenses, Investment Gains and Foreign Exchange Differences
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest income, received dividends, asset disposal results, donations, penalties, and foreign exchange gains or losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Administrative penalties and tax late fees are not tax deductible; add them back outside this box. Charitable donations are capped at 12% of annual accounting profit. Foreign-exchange gains realized from cross-border settlements are taxable; unrealized gains may be subject to adjustment under tax rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8: Tax Adjustments, Add-backs and Special Tax Adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule of permanent and temporary differences: nondeductible expenditures, tax-exempt income, depreciation differences, impairment provisions, thin-capitalization interest disallowance, and transfer pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a WFOE, add back excessive net interest paid to foreign related lenders above the 2:1 debt-to-equity thin-capitalization safe harbor for non-financial enterprises. Add back intercompany service or royalty payments lacking substance. If a prior year transfer pricing adjustment increases taxable income, include it here under the special tax adjustment schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 9: Taxable Income and Applicable Tax Rate
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit adjusted to taxable income, then application of the statutory or preferential EIT rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use 25% unless the WFOE has a valid tax filing for High and New Technology Enterprise status (15%), Small Low-Profit status, or an applicable encouraged-industry preferential rate. Preferential rates must be self-certified with supporting program filings; unauthorized use creates tax-exposure risk.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 10: Tax Payable, Credits, Prepayments and Final Settlement
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross EIT, foreign tax credits, quarterly prepayments, and final balance due or refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits may be claimed for foreign-source income but cannot exceed the PRC tax payable on that foreign-source income. Dividend withholding tax on profits distributed by the WFOE to its foreign parent is not paid on the annual EIT return; it is separately withheld and reported through the non-resident withholding system.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Mandatory disclosure of all controlled transactions: tangible goods, intangible assets, financial assets, intercompany services, and cost-sharing arrangements. Include transaction amounts, pricing policies, and transfer pricing methods.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File this schedule even when no Local or Master File is required. State whether contemporaneous benchmark studies exist and that documents will be available within 20 days if the tax authority requires access. False or omitted related-party disclosures attract separate penalties and increased audit risk.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual EIT return: the tax authority issues a deadline and may impose a fine up to RMB 2,000 for ordinary late filing, and up to RMB 10,000 for serious non-filing. Underpaid tax carries a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% of the outstanding tax (approximately 18.25% per annum). Tax evasion via false return or concealment gives a civil penalty of 50% to five times the underpaid tax. Criminal fraud arises when the evaded tax exceeds RMB 50,000 and represents more than 10% of the tax payable; responsible persons face fines and imprisonment up to seven years under Criminal Law Article 201.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory withholding income tax on dividends distributed by a Chinese WFOE to a non-resident foreign enterprise shareholder that has no establishment or place of business in China.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced dividend withholding rate under a Bilateral Double Tax Treaty, the foreign parent must: (1) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its home jurisdiction, authenticated/apostilled and translated into Chinese where required; (2) prove beneficial ownership of the dividends and that the parent is not a conduit or agent; (3) demonstrate direct equity ownership meeting the treaty threshold (commonly 10% or 25% depending on treaty) and any minimum holding period (typically 12 months); (4) submit the Non-Resident Enterprise Tax Treaty Benefit Application Form and supporting evidence to the domestic withholding agent or competent tax authority before the dividend is paid; and (5) allow the withholding agent to apply the reduced treaty rate only after approval. If treaty relief is not applied before distribution, the full 10% statutory withholding tax is remitted and a refund/reliable-credit application may be pursued under the tax administration rules.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The statutory PRC withholding income tax rate on interest and royalties payable to a non-resident enterprise is 10%. Royalty payments also attract VAT at 6% through the non-resident VAT process. Under applicable DTAs, interest treaty rates commonly fall to 0% or 10%, and royalty treaty rates commonly fall to 5% or 10%, depending on beneficial ownership, licensing substance, and specific treaty provisions. The parent must still produce a TRC, beneficial ownership evidence, and treaty application forms to enjoy any reduced rate.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A Chinese Local File is required for a tax year if the enterprise has controlled transactions exceeding: (i) RMB 200 million for tangible property transfers; (ii) RMB 100 million for intangible property transfers; (iii) RMB 100 million for financial asset transfers; (iv) RMB 100 million for related-party services; or (v) RMB 40 million for other controlled transactions. A Master File is required when aggregate annual related-party transaction amounts reach RMB 1 billion. The annual related-party transactions schedule must be filed regardless of these thresholds, and contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation must be submitted within 20 days upon tax authority demand.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China does not apply Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations, but the tax authorities apply substance-over-form, beneficial ownership, place-of-effective-management, and Controlled Foreign Company rules. For a WFOE engaged in direct online retail, the core income-generating activities must be verifiable in China: local management and employees, procurement decisions, inventory warehousing, order fulfilment, payment collection through Stripe/Affirm rails, after-sales service, and substantive e-commerce platform contracts. A letterbox company with no local staff or functions will be denied treaty benefits, may be treated as having no genuine Chinese operating substance, and is exposed to general anti-avoidance rule adjustments, deemed dividend reclassification, and 10% withholding plus interest and penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE pays excessive management fees, trademark royalties, e-commerce platform charges, or technical service fees to a foreign related party while performing little or no actual local profit-producing activity. The fees are unjustified by functional analysis, no Local File is prepared, and no arm's length benchmark exists.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 41 and Article 48 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law authorize re-assessment at arm's length; Administrative Measures for Special Tax Adjustments allow corresponding income adjustments and interest charges. Tax Collection Law Article 63 imposes a penalty of 50% to five times the underpaid tax plus daily 0.05% late surcharge. If the scheme is found fraudulent, criminal prosecution under Criminal Law Article 201 may follow.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who intentionally design sham related-party pricing can be personally liable through piercing of the corporate veil under Company Law Article 20 where the corporate form is abused to evade tax or harm creditors. Personal civil liability extends to restitution of the wrongfully shifted profits and unpaid tax. Criminal liability for tax evasion can result in imprisonment up to seven years, monetary fines, and exit restrictions on the legal representative through the tax authority's border-control notification mechanism.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company Without Economic Substance and Treaty Shopping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE operates as a mailbox entity with no employees, no local management, no purchase or fulfillment functions, no substantive decision-making, and no verifiable core income-generating activities in China. It nevertheless claims reduced DTA withholding rates for dividend repatriation and domestic EIT advantages as a Chinese resident.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The General Anti-Avoidance Rule under Article 47 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law and the Beneficial Ownership rules under State Taxation Administration circulars allow the tax authority to deny treaty benefits, re-characterize the entity, or impose the full 10% statutory dividend withholding tax. Denial of treaty relief, together with underpaid tax surcharges and administrative penalties, may be applied. Tax Collection Law Article 44 permits the legal representative to be prohibited from leaving China until tax liabilities are discharged.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners who sign false treaty-benefit declarations or establish the WFOE to abuse treaty relief face personal civil liability for restitution and tax penalties. Under Company Law Article 20, the corporate veil may be pierced if the entity is a mere instrument for tax avoidance, exposing directors' personal assets. Repeated treaty shopping may trigger criminal fraud charges; senior management may also face public tax-honesty blacklisting and travel bans.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Criminal Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Corporate Income Tax Filing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE deliberately omits online sales revenue collected through Stripe and Affirm BNPL rails, submits a false annual EIT return showing zero or understated income, destroys accounting books, and fails to file the annual related-party transactions schedule.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax Collection Law Article 63 imposes a penalty of 50% to five times the underpaid tax and daily late surcharge. Criminal Law Article 201 creates criminal liability for tax evasion where the amount evaded is relatively large and exceeds 10% of the tax due; large-scale evasion carries up to three years' imprisonment; huge amounts carry three to seven years' imprisonment with fines. Exit-exit controls and asset seizure are authorized for unpaid major tax liabilities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Because tax evasion is committed by the WFOE as a legal entity, the directors, legal representative, actual controller, and CFO who initiated or knowingly approved the false return can be held personally responsible. The court may pierce the corporate veil under Company Law Article 20 and order personal civil restitution of the evaded tax and penalties. Criminal convictions result in direct imprisonment, fines, disqualification from serving as directors, and post-release restrictions on senior management roles.
